short: The East India Company was established by royal charter to trade in the Indian Ocean, eventually becoming a dominant global colonial power.
full:
On 31 December 1600, Elizabeth I granted a royal charter to the "Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies." Initially formed to break the Spanish and Portuguese monopoly on the lucrative spice trade, the joint-stock company dispatched early fleets that successfully established factories in places like Bantam.

Although its early ventures yielded mixed financial results against entrenched Dutch competition, the Company laid the groundwork for massive institutional expansion. By the eighteenth century, it would evolve from a mere trading venture into an aggressive imperial agent that controlled vast territories across the Indian subcontinent and generated half of all British trade.
